column2: Living docs current and consistent with the code [SO2]
column6: The living docs (docs/requirements.md, docs/design.md, docs/rfcs/ or docs/adr/, docs/risks.md, README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md plus the AI context file (AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md)) exist, are in the PDF matching the named commit, and pass the spot-check: docs/design.md describes the system that exists, requirements carry acceptance criteria for current priorities, and the quickstart is accurate.
column9: The docs exist but one or more have drifted from the code, are missing sections or missing from the PDF (unless an NDA walkthrough stands in), are not rendered, or read as written for the grader rather than for the team.
column12: Living docs are largely missing, stale, or inconsistent with the repository, the PDF carries none of them without an NDA walkthrough standing in, or the living docs in the PDF do not match the named commit (a sanitized PDF differs only in what was redacted).

column6: Every gate item for this checkpoint is met: the stories docs/requirements.md marks for this term run end to end at the named commit against real components rather than stubs, the CI run linked on the cover ran the tests on the named commit including a test for at least one of those stories, docs/risks.md records a scheduled session with a real user, and the Definition of Done and the Contribution Norm in CONTRIBUTING.md reflect the winter charter refresh.
column9: One gate item is unmet or only demonstrable with help, and docs/risks.md gives an owner and a week to close it (e.g., one marked story still runs against a stub, no test covers a marked story, the real-user session is planned but has no week or participant yet, or CONTRIBUTING.md neither changed since Repo Checkpoint 2 nor says the refresh kept it).
column12: Two or more gate items are unmet, or one is unmet with no docs/risks.md entry giving an owner and a week to close it.

column2: Build health and safety net: CI, tests, quickstart, gates [SO6]
column3: CI passes on the named commit and runs the tests on every pull request, tests exist and test something real, quickstart works, and the checks match how much the team delegates (review gates on the paths that are hard to undo, somewhere to exercise changes before users get them, a documented rollback path)
column6: CI passed on the named commit and runs the tests on every pull request; at least one test would fail if the feature it covers broke; a grader can follow the quickstart cold. The checks match how much the team delegates: review gates on the changes that are expensive to undo (schema, authentication, deployment, migrations), changes exercised somewhere other than production before they reach users (a staging or preview environment, a store beta track, a bench device, a run on sample data), and a documented rollback path.
column9: CI and tests exist and the quickstart mostly works, but the checks have visible gaps relative to how the team works: no gate on a hard-to-undo path, or no rollback story.
column12: CI is absent or red, tests do not test anything real, the quickstart does not work, or changes reach production with no gate and no rollback path.

column3: RFCs/ADRs recorded, single risk register alive and ranked
column6: RFCs and ADRs are recorded with outcomes; the single risk register (docs/risks.md) is alive, ranked, and has owners; no duplicate registers elsewhere.
column9: Decisions and risks are tracked but incompletely: some decisions unrecorded, ranking or owners missing, or the register has not moved since the last checkpoint.
column12: No recorded decisions, or no usable risk register.

column3: work is attributable per student (code through PRs authored and reviewed under real accounts, other work where CONTRIBUTING.md says it lives, contribution lines in sprint notes matching the record), and the history is one a maintainer could inherit
column6: Each student's work is attributable over the period: code through reviewed PRs under real accounts, other work where the Contribution Norm in CONTRIBUTING.md says it lives, and the contribution lines match that record. History is clean: nothing lands on the default branch outside a pull request, no live secrets or build artifacts are in the history (if a secret leaked, it was revoked or rotated, and the commit that removed it says so), and commit messages say what changed.
column9: Most students' work is traceable, but some of it cannot be attributed, or the history has hygiene problems (direct commits to the default branch, uninformative messages, committed artifacts).
column12: Contribution cannot be traced to individuals over the period, or a secret was committed and never rotated.
